title: Anatomy of a Bank Fixed Deposit: Rate, Compounding and Exit Rules
brief: Covers how bank fixed-deposit rates, compounding conventions, premature-withdrawal penalties and joint-holder options work in India. Answers what an advertised rate actually yields once compounding and exit terms are accounted for. Readers finish able to compare two fixed-deposit offers on genuinely equivalent terms.

title: Recurring Deposits and Savings Accounts: The Quiet Cost of Idle Cash
brief: Covers monthly-average-balance rules, savings-account rate regimes and recurring-deposit compounding, contrasting both with short-duration alternatives. Answers how much money should realistically sit in transaction accounts. Readers can size a working-capital buffer and park the excess deliberately.

title: Corporate and NBFC Fixed Deposits: Reading the Risk Behind the Extra Yield
brief: Covers how company and NBFC deposits are issued, which regulator supervises whom, and what ratings and public filings reveal. Answers whether a higher quoted rate compensates for real default risk. Readers finish able to check an offer against balance-sheet evidence.

title: Cooperative Bank Deposits and What Deposit Insurance Really Covers
brief: Covers the constraints of cooperative and small-finance bank deposits, including the statutory insurance cover per depositor per bank and how claims are settled. Answers how worried a saver should be about bank failure. Readers can structure deposits across institutions accordingly.

title: Deposit Insurance Mechanics: Rights, Exclusions and Claim Timelines
brief: Covers deposit-insurance computation across accounts, joint and trust deposits, and the entities whose deposits are excluded from cover. Answers how a payout would actually reach a depositor after a bank failure. Readers finish able to apportion deposits to stay within insured limits.

title: Treasury Bills as the Risk-Free Anchor of Indian Finance
brief: Covers Treasury bill tenors, discount pricing and how auction cut-offs translate into effective annual yields. Answers how to read an auction result and what the resulting number means for savers. Readers can compute a T-bill's effective annual return before bidding.

title: Dated G-Secs and the Coupon Myth: Price, Yield and Total Return
brief: Covers how dated government securities trade, why the coupon is not the return, and how price changes dominate outcomes for buyers. Answers what a retail investor actually earns from a G-sec. Readers finish able to reason about a purchased security's full return.

title: State Development Loans: Fiscal Risk Priced in Yield
brief: Covers state development loan issuance through RBI auctions, their quasi-sovereign treatment and the yield spread over central government securities. Answers what that spread compensates for and what it ignores. Readers can judge whether an SDL suits a conservative portfolio.

title: RBI Retail Direct: Bidding in Auctions Without a Broker
brief: Covers Retail Direct account opening, primary auction bidding, secondary-market purchase and settlement mechanics for government securities and T-bills. Answers what a retail investor can and cannot do on the platform. Readers finish able to participate in an auction directly.

title: G-Sec Secondary Market Liquidity: Why Some Bonds Are Hard to Sell
brief: Covers on-the-run versus off-the-run securities, trade reporting and how bid-ask spreads widen away from benchmark tenors. Answers why a government bond can still be difficult to exit. Readers can favour liquid tenors when buying with resale in mind.

title: Money-Market Versus Capital-Market Instruments: The One-Year Boundary
brief: Covers the boundary between money-market instruments such as Treasury bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit, and longer capital-market bonds. Answers which instrument fits a given cash horizon. Readers can map a surplus to the right market segment.

title: Commercial Paper and the Rollover Dependence Problem
brief: Covers how Indian companies issue commercial paper, the role of credit ratings, and the manner in which issuers depend on continuous refinancing. Answers what happens when the market freezes. Readers can assess rollover risk before buying short-dated paper.

title: Certificates of Deposit: Bank Wholesale Funding for the Retail Investor
brief: Covers certificate of deposit issuance by banks, ticket sizes, secondary-market quotes and how CD yields respond to liquidity conditions. Answers whether a CD adds anything over a plain bank deposit. Readers finish able to evaluate CD quotes against their alternatives.

title: Call Money, TREPS and the Collateralised Interbank Market
brief: Covers overnight borrowing markets, the shift towards collateralised TREPS trades and how these rates transmit monetary policy. Answers how short-end rates are actually set. Readers can interpret overnight-rate movements reported in the financial press.

title: Repo, Reverse Repo and the RBI Liquidity Corridor Explained
brief: Covers the policy repo, reverse repo and marginal standing facility as a corridor, plus variable-rate operations. Answers why money-market rates rarely stray far outside that band. Readers can connect policy announcements to deposit and lending rates.

title: Bond Pricing from Cash Flows to Present Value
brief: Covers discounting each coupon and principal repayment at a chosen yield to derive a bond price, including annual and semi-annual conventions used in India. Answers why two bonds with identical coupons can price differently. Readers can price a simple bond by hand.

title: Yield to Maturity Versus Current Yield: Which Number to Trust
brief: Covers the difference between coupon, current yield and yield to maturity, including the reinvestment assumptions embedded in each. Answers which figure a buyer of an Indian corporate bond should quote. Readers can compare two bonds on a consistent yield basis.

title: Clean and Dirty Prices: Accrued Interest in Indian Bond Trades
brief: Covers accrued-interest computation, ex-interest and cum-interest trading dates, and why the settlement value differs from the quoted price. Answers how much cash a bond purchase actually requires. Readers can verify the figures on a debt trade contract note.

title: Macaulay Duration and the Timing of Cash Flows
brief: Covers duration as a weighted-average time to receive a bond's cash flows, and how coupon size and maturity change it. Answers why a long bond is not proportionately riskier than a short one. Readers can interpret a duration figure meaningfully rather than mechanically.

title: Modified Duration: Pricing a Bond's Interest-Rate Sensitivity
brief: Covers the percentage price change implied by modified duration for a small yield move, and the conditions under which the approximation weakens. Answers how much a portfolio could fall when yields rise. Readers can run a first-order rate-shock estimate.

title: Convexity: Where Duration-Based Estimates Break Down
brief: Covers second-order price sensitivity, the asymmetry between yield rises and falls, and how barbell and bullet portfolios differ in convexity. Answers why large rate moves surprise duration-based forecasts. Readers can rank bonds by convexity when choosing between similar yields.

title: DV01 and the Practice of Rate Hedging
brief: Covers the value of a one-basis-point move per unit of exposure, and how it aggregates across a fixed-income portfolio. Answers how many futures or securities would offset a given rate exposure. Readers can compute and explain a simple hedge ratio.

title: Yield Curve Shapes: Steep, Flat and Inverted Signals
brief: Covers normal, flat and inverted Indian yield curves, the segments that matter most, and the predictive claims made about them. Answers what a curve move is really saying about growth and inflation expectations. Readers can read curve charts critically.

title: Term Structure Theories: Expectations, Liquidity and Segmentation
brief: Covers the expectations hypothesis, liquidity-premium and market-segmentation explanations for why long rates usually exceed short rates. Answers which explanation fits Indian sovereign markets best. Readers can evaluate claims about forward rates and curve steepness.

title: Decomposing a Credit Spread: Default, Liquidity and Risk Premium
brief: Covers how a corporate bond spread over the government curve reflects expected default loss, illiquidity and investor risk aversion. Answers which component dominates under Indian conditions. Readers can question whether a quoted spread is adequate compensation.

title: What Moves Indian Corporate Bond Spreads
brief: Covers issuer quality, issue size, investor base and macro stress as drivers of spreads between Indian corporate bonds and government securities. Answers why two similarly rated issuers can trade at different yields. Readers can compare spreads with a structured checklist.

title: How Indian Credit Rating Agencies Arrive at a Rating
brief: Covers the rating process, business-risk and financial-risk assessment, support assumptions and outlook conventions used by Indian rating agencies. Answers what a rating does and does not certify. Readers can use ratings sceptically rather than absolutely.

title: Rating Migration and the Cost of Notch Risk
brief: Covers downgrade and upgrade migration patterns, multi-notch moves and the price damage that ratings changes cause in Indian bond markets. Answers why an intention to hold to maturity does not immunise a portfolio. Readers can monitor holdings for migration risk.

title: Secured and Unsecured Debentures: What Recovery Depends On
brief: Covers security creation, charge registration, guarantees and the recovery hierarchy that applies to Indian debentures. Answers what actually stands behind a promise to pay. Readers can compare recoverability between two issues carrying similar coupons.

title: Debenture Trustees and the Enforcement of Covenants
brief: Covers trustee appointment, covenant design, security-cover monitoring and the trustee's duties when an issuer defaults. Answers who acts for dispersed bondholders when trouble arrives. Readers know what to check in trustee disclosures before investing.

title: Embedded Put and Call Options in Indian Debentures
brief: Covers issuer calls and investor puts, their effect on achieved yield, and exit mechanics in the Indian corporate bond market. Answers how embedded options change the return that actually accrues. Readers can evaluate a yield-to-call rather than trusting headline yield.

title: Perpetual Bonds: Yield to Call Is the Only Yield That Matters
brief: Covers perpetual bond structures, call schedules and the extension risk investors accept in exchange for a higher coupon. Answers what happens when the issuer declines to call. Readers can compute a yield-to-call for a perpetual instrument.

title: AT1 Bonds and the Write-Down Mechanics Investors Often Miss
brief: Covers additional tier-1 instruments, coupon discretion, trigger events and the ability to write down principal. Answers how an apparently safe bank bond can lose most of its value. Readers can identify AT1 risk language in an offer document.

title: Tier-2 Bonds in the Bank Capital Stack
brief: Covers the role of tier-2 bonds in meeting regulatory capital requirements, their subordination and their typical features in India. Answers how tier-2 paper differs from a bank deposit or senior bond. Readers can classify a bank capital issue correctly.

title: Market-Linked Debentures: Structure, Payoff and Tax Treatment
brief: Covers how market-linked debentures tie returns to an underlying index while capping gains and losses, and the tax treatment that reshaped issuance. Answers why MLDs get sold as debt with equity-like marketing. Readers can dissect an MLD term sheet.

title: NCD Coupon Mechanics, Record Dates and Tax Deduction at Source
brief: Covers how Indian non-convertible debenture interest is computed, credited and taxed at source, including cumulative and periodic payout options. Answers what the investor actually receives each cycle. Readers can compute a net coupon from a term sheet.

title: Municipal Bonds in India: Credit Without a Sovereign Guarantee
brief: Covers issuer types, revenue pledges, credit enhancement and the limited secondary market for Indian municipal debt. Answers whether a municipal bond offers genuinely risk-free exposure. Readers can assess a municipal issue on its own credit merits.

title: Credit-Enhanced and Guaranteed Bonds: Where the Risk Really Sits
brief: Covers partial guarantees, structured payment mechanisms and comfort letters used in Indian bond issues. Answers whether credit enhancement shifts risk or merely obscures it. Readers can separate the guarantor's credit from the issuer's own.

title: Securitisation: How a Loan Pool Becomes a Bond
brief: Covers the pooling of loans, tranching, servicing arrangements and the flow of collections to investors. Answers how a pass-through structure isolates underlying credit risk. Readers can read a pool's basic cash-flow waterfall.

title: Pass-Through Certificates: Yield, Prepayment and Credit Layers
brief: Covers how Indian pass-through certificates are priced, the effect of prepayments on different tranches, and the credit-enhancement layers underneath. Answers which tranche bears first loss. Readers can evaluate a certificate on structure rather than yield alone.

title: Mortgage-Backed Securities in the Indian Market
brief: Covers residential mortgage securitisation by banks and housing finance companies, and what makes Indian mortgage pools behave differently from their global counterparts. Answers why prepayment assumptions dominate valuation here. Readers can follow a mortgage pool's amortisation logic.

title: Invoice Discounting and TReDS: Financing Business Receivables
brief: Covers the mechanics of invoice discounting on TReDS platforms, the role of accepting corporates and the financier's recourse. Answers how a financier's return and risk are shaped by the structure. Readers can evaluate a receivables-financing opportunity.

title: Factoring Versus Invoice Discounting: Why Recourse Still Matters
brief: Covers the distinction between factoring with recourse, non-recourse factoring and plain bill discounting in the Indian context. Answers who bears a debtor's default in each structure. Readers can match a financing route to a specific cash-flow need.

title: PD, LGD and EAD: A Practitioner's Framework for Credit Loss
brief: Covers probability of default, loss given default, exposure at default and how their product forms expected credit loss. Answers how to translate a lending proposition into a loss-adjusted expected return. Readers can model a retail credit opportunity coherently.

title: Expected Credit Loss Modelling for a Bond Portfolio
brief: Covers scenario-based loss provisioning, recovery timing and the difference between expected and unexpected loss. Answers how to embed credit losses into a portfolio's expected return estimate. Readers can build a simple loss-adjusted yield calculation.

title: Default and Recovery in Indian Corporate Credit
brief: Covers historical recovery patterns, the role of security and the time value lost during resolution. Answers what a bondholder might realistically recover from a defaulted Indian issuer. Readers can set recovery assumptions rather than assuming full repayment.

title: The IBC Resolution Timeline: What Creditors Should Expect
brief: Covers corporate insolvency resolution process steps, committee-of-creditors voting and the statutory timeline framework under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. Answers why recoveries take years. Readers can interpret resolution news accurately.

title: Asset Reconstruction Companies and Security Receipts Explained
brief: Covers how Indian asset reconstruction companies acquire stressed loans, issue security receipts and share recoveries with investors. Answers what a buyer of security receipts actually owns. Readers can assess the risk embedded in distressed-loan funds.

title: Distressed Debt Investing: Buying Claims at a Discount
brief: Covers how stressed Indian debt trades, pricing conventions and the legal routes to recovery or control. Answers where the return in distressed debt actually comes from. Readers can sketch a distressed thesis and its failure cases.

title: Private Credit Funds: Yield Premiums and Their Limits
brief: Covers the Indian private-credit universe, deal structures, security packages and the yield premium over public bonds. Answers what risks justify that premium. Readers can interrogate a private-credit proposition systematically before committing capital.

title: Venture Debt Term Sheets: Warrants, Covenants and Cost
brief: Covers how Indian venture-debt lenders structure interest, warrant coverage, milestones and default triggers for startup borrowers. Answers what a founder or a lender gives up in the bargain. Readers can read a venture-debt term sheet critically.

title: Mezzanine and Unitranche Structures for Indian Borrowers
brief: Covers layered debt structures, subordination, warrants and blended pricing used in Indian mid-market financings. Answers where mezzanine sits in the capital stack and when unitranche replaces it. Readers can compare the economics of both structures.

title: Credit Default Swaps: A Thin Indian Market Explained
brief: Covers the RBI framework permitting credit default swaps on corporate bonds, eligible participants and the market's limited depth. Answers why CDS has not become a mainstream hedging tool in India. Readers can judge when a CDS is practically usable.

title: G-Sec STRIPS and Zero-Coupon Structures
brief: Covers the separation of government securities into coupon and principal strips, their pricing as zero-coupon instruments and their liquidity. Answers who benefits from stripping. Readers can match a strip's maturity to a known future liability.

title: Floating-Rate Bonds and Benchmark Linking in India
brief: Covers floating-rate coupons referenced to Treasury bill or repo benchmarks, reset mechanics and the basis risk that remains. Answers whether floating-rate debt truly removes interest-rate risk. Readers can evaluate a floater's reset terms.

title: Inflation-Indexed Bonds: Protection and Its Shadow
brief: Covers the design of Indian inflation-indexed government bonds, indexation conventions and how to interpret the quoted real yield. Answers why these bonds attract less retail interest than expected. Readers can compute a real yield from quoted terms.

title: Tax-Free Bonds: Yield, Liquidity and the Issuance Pipeline
brief: Covers tax-free bond issuers, coupon treatment, secondary-market pricing and the scarcity that followed reduced issuance. Answers whether a lower tax-free coupon beats a taxable alternative. Readers can compare the two on a post-tax basis.

title: Reading a Bond Information Memorandum Before Investing
brief: Covers the sections of an Indian bond offer document that matter: issuer financials, security, covenants, use of proceeds and exit terms. Answers where key risks hide in boilerplate. Readers can complete a structured pre-investment review.

title: Bond Market Risks Beyond Credit: Rate, Liquidity and Reinvestment
brief: Covers interest-rate, liquidity, reinvestment and inflation risks, and how they interact inside Indian debt portfolios. Answers why supposedly safe bonds can still deliver disappointing outcomes. Readers can name each risk present in their own holdings.

title: Building a Starter Bond Portfolio from Deposits to G-Secs
brief: Covers sequencing a first fixed-income portfolio across deposits, Treasury bills, government securities and high-grade corporate bonds. Answers how much credit and duration risk a beginner should reasonably take. Readers can draft an allocation with explicit liquidity layers.

title: Small-Cap Equity and the Twenty Percent Threshold
brief: Investigates whether small-cap Indian equities can deliver above 20% p.a., separating the size effect from liquidity and drawdown costs. Answers who should attempt this and with what position sizing. Readers can judge the claim against their own risk capacity.

title: Micro-Cap Liquidity Crises as Entry Points
brief: Investigates buying micro-cap Indian shares during liquidity droughts, when prices disconnect from business fundamentals. Answers how to separate temporary dislocation from terminal decline. Readers can build entry and exit rules that respect thin liquidity.

title: Momentum Strategies in Indian Equities
brief: Investigates systematic momentum portfolios in Indian equities and whether turnover costs leave anything above 20% p.a. Answers how crowding and sharp reversals erode the edge. Readers can evaluate a momentum product's realistic net potential.

title: Concentrated Equity Portfolios: Conviction and Its Costs
brief: Investigates concentrated Indian portfolios holding a handful of businesses, where above-20% p.a. outcomes coexist with permanent-loss risk. Answers how conviction positions should be sized. Readers can structure concentrated bets without endangering overall solvency.

title: Special Situations Investing in Indian Markets
brief: Investigates Indian special situations: mergers, court-approved schemes, capital-structure changes and regulatory outcomes. Answers how event timelines determine returns above ordinary equity averages. Readers can map an event's payoff table before committing capital.

title: SME IPO Investing on the NSE and BSE SME Platforms
brief: Investigates SME IPOs on Indian exchange platforms, where small issues and thin floats create outsized moves in both directions. Answers what the boom narratives skip in due diligence. Readers can screen an SME issue on fundamentals and float.

title: Promoter-Change and Turnaround Plays
brief: Investigates Indian equities where ownership changes or operational turnarounds promise re-ratings above 20% p.a. Answers what evidence distinguishes a credible plan from a story. Readers can build a turnaround scorecard of observable milestones.

title: Demerger and Scheme-of-Arrangement Arbitrage
brief: Investigates India's demerger arbitrage, where parts of a business get valued separately after a court-approved split. Answers how to estimate when the value unlocks. Readers can weigh a scheme's expected payoff against execution and timing risk.

title: Rights-Issue Arbitrage Mechanics
brief: Investigates the arithmetic of Indian rights issues: entitlement value, renunciation trading and the effective entry price after subscribing. Answers whether a visible discount is genuinely exploitable. Readers can compute a rights position's true cost.

title: Buyback Tender Windows and Acceptance Arbitrage
brief: Investigates Indian buyback tender windows, acceptance ratios and the small-shareholder reservation. Answers how a tender bid converts a discount into a realised above-market outcome. Readers can size a buyback arbitrage position with clear failure limits.

title: Closed-End Fund Discounts: Opportunity or Value Trap
brief: Investigates closed-end Indian funds trading below net asset value, and the paths by which discounts narrow or persist until maturity. Answers what prevents discounts from closing on their own. Readers can distinguish a genuine opportunity from a structural discount.

title: NCD Yield Spikes During Credit Stress
brief: Investigates buying Indian corporate NCDs when credit stress pushes quoted yields above 20% p.a. Answers how to separate panic pricing from impending default. Readers can define the conditions under which such purchases are defensible.

title: High-Yield NCD Portfolio Construction
brief: Investigates building portfolios of higher-yielding Indian NCDs where individual defaults are expected but portfolio outcomes can exceed 20% p.a. Answers how many positions diversification realistically requires. Readers can set position limits and loss buckets.

title: Private Credit Yield Premiums Outside Public Markets
brief: Investigates Indian private-credit funds targeting yields above public bond markets, the security packages behind them and their illiquidity cost. Answers what the premium is genuinely paid for. Readers can benchmark an offer against its embedded risks.

title: Venture Capital Fund Returns and Their Power Law
brief: Investigates how Indian venture funds produce above-20% p.a. returns at fund level, and why most portfolios depend on a few outcomes. Answers how to read a track record properly. Readers can evaluate a fund's return concentration before committing.

title: Angel Investing Economics and Its Pitfalls
brief: Investigates Indian angel investing, where exit multiples above 20% p.a. are possible only across many write-offs. Answers what position sizing and follow-on discipline the mathematics demands. Readers can assemble a realistic angel programme.

title: Pre-IPO and Unlisted Share Marketplaces
brief: Investigates India's unlisted share market: valuation gaps before listing and the custody, disclosure and tax problems that accompany them. Answers where promised excess returns actually come from. Readers can scrutinise an unlisted offer before wiring money.

title: SME Business Acquisitions and Cash-Flow Yields
brief: Investigates acquiring small Indian businesses at cash-flow yields above 20% p.a. on purchase price, and the operational work that yield demands. Answers how buyers verify earnings in informal settings. Readers can draft acquisition criteria for a structured search.

title: Search Funds and Succession Buyouts in India
brief: Investigates the search-fund model adapted to India, where young operators buy businesses from retiring owners with investor backing. Answers how returns above 20% p.a. are underwritten. Readers can assess a search-fund partnership offer.

title: Revenue-Based Financing: Investor Returns and Caps
brief: Investigates revenue-based financing in India, where repayment is tied to monthly receipts rather than fixed instalments. Answers how caps and multiples produce lender returns above 20% p.a. when seasoning behaves. Readers can model a revenue-financing tape.

title: Franchise Economics and Ownership Returns
brief: Investigates owning Indian franchise outlets, where unit-level returns can exceed 20% p.a. on invested capital when location and format work. Answers which costs the pitch materials omit. Readers can underwrite a franchise unit purchase end to end.

title: Real-Estate Development Margins and Their Cycles
brief: Investigates Indian real-estate development projects where developer-level returns exceed 20% p.a. in good cycles, and where leverage turns them negative. Answers how to read a project's true profit pool. Readers can assess a development proposal critically.

title: Leveraged Property and Rental Yields
brief: Investigates leveraged Indian property positions where rental yield plus appreciation must clear financing cost before exceeding 20% p.a. Answers how leverage magnifies outcomes in both directions. Readers can stress-test a leveraged purchase decision.

title: Fractional Ownership Platforms and Their Return Claims
brief: Investigates fractional real-estate platforms promising yields above 20% p.a., testing those claims against the SEBI small and medium REIT framework. Answers what protections a private platform lacks. Readers can classify an offer as regulated or purely contractual.

title: Distressed Asset Purchase and Land Banking
brief: Investigates acquiring distressed Indian property and land from over-leveraged sellers, then holding through approval and market cycles. Answers how carrying costs and title problems determine outcomes. Readers can estimate the all-in cost of a distress purchase.

title: Data-Centre Yieldco Economics
brief: Investigates Indian data-centre and digital-infrastructure yieldcos, where contracted cash flows plus growth can compound above 20% p.a. for equity holders. Answers which contractual and counterparty risks the distribution depends on. Readers can evaluate a yieldco proposition.

title: Gold-Loan NBFC Equity Cycles
brief: Investigates Indian gold-loan NBFC equities, where gold-price cycles and borrowing costs swing earnings sharply. Answers when the cycle supports above-20% p.a. equity returns and when it inverts. Readers can track the operating drivers that matter.

title: Hospital and Pharma Capex Cycles
brief: Investigates the Indian hospital and pharmaceutical capex cycle, where new capacity drives multi-year operating leverage. Answers how to time exposure around utilisation curves. Readers can link capex disclosures to future earnings potential.

title: Commodity Cycle Equity Plays
brief: Investigates Indian commodity producers, where cycle peaks have produced returns above 20% p.a. and cycle turns erase them. Answers which cost-curve signals distinguish survivors from casualties. Readers can place commodity exposure with explicit cycle awareness.

title: Carbon Credits and Natural-Capital Returns
brief: Investigates carbon-credit and natural-capital projects in India, where verification integrity and demand determine whether returns above 20% p.a. are achievable. Answers what makes a credit real and bankable. Readers can screen carbon projects for substance.

title: Timber and Plantation Economics Over Long Rotations
brief: Investigates Indian timber and plantation investments with long rotations, where internal rates above 20% p.a. depend on survival, species and fire or theft losses. Answers how to model the holding period honestly. Readers can evaluate a plantation offer.

title: Agri-Land Leasing Yields: Income Versus Total Return
brief: Investigates leasing Indian farmland and the net yield after taxes, water availability and tenant arrangements. Answers whether the income alone can approach 20% p.a. or only total-return claims can. Readers can compute a realistic farm-lease return.

title: P2P Portfolio Yield Construction Above Twenty Percent
brief: Investigates constructing P2P portfolios on RBI-licensed platforms where gross lending rates exceed 20% p.a. before defaults and taxes. Answers what net yield is realistic after losses. Readers can set diversification and loss assumptions deliberately.

title: Invoice Discounting Yield Tapes and Delay Risk
brief: Investigates receivables-finance tapes in India where annualised yields above 20% p.a. are quoted on short-dated invoices. Answers how debtor concentration and payment delays reduce the realised figure. Readers can audit an invoice tape before funding it.

title: Option Selling: Premium Harvesting and Tail Risk
brief: Investigates systematic option selling in Indian markets, where premium income can annualise above 20% p.a. until one adverse move erases months. Answers how to size the tail. Readers can stress-test a premium-selling plan before deploying it.

title: Volatility Arbitrage in Indian Options
brief: Investigates volatility-based option strategies in India, where gaps between implied and realised volatility must clear costs before exceeding 20% p.a. Answers how to measure that edge honestly. Readers can estimate a volatility trade's breakevens.

title: Leveraged Directional Trading and Ruin Risk
brief: Investigates leveraged futures and options trading marketed as a route to outsized returns, and the ruin mathematics that make sustained 20% plus compounding rare. Answers how leverage changes survival probability. Readers can evaluate a trading plan's survivability.

title: Sports and Entertainment Royalty Financing
brief: Investigates royalty and revenue-share financing of Indian sports leagues, films and music catalogues, where underwritten returns can exceed 20% p.a. Answers what makes a title's revenue predictable. Readers can assess a royalty proposal's downside.

title: Solar and Waste-Processing Business Economics
brief: Investigates owning Indian solar assets and waste-processing businesses, where contracted offtake and tipping fees can support above-20% p.a. returns in favourable cases. Answers which counterparty and regulatory risks dominate. Readers can build a project model.

title: Gold and Silver Cycle Trading
brief: Investigates trading Indian gold and silver through cycle swings, where strong years exceed 20% p.a. and reversals unwind them. Answers how currency and import-duty changes interact with local prices. Readers can frame a cycle position with stop discipline.

title: Digital-Asset High-Beta Cycles and Position Sizing
brief: Investigates digital-asset exposure through India-accessible routes, where cycles have produced gains far above 20% p.a. alongside deep drawdowns. Answers what position sizing keeps a broader portfolio intact. Readers can bound a crypto allocation rationally.

title: REIT and InvIT Total Return Stacking
brief: Investigates REIT and InvIT positions where distributions, asset-level growth and re-rating together can exceed 20% p.a. in favourable cycles. Answers how leverage and acquisitions alter the stack. Readers can decompose a trust's expected total return.

title: Toll-Road and Transmission InvIT Returns
brief: Investigates Indian toll-road and power-transmission InvITs, whose contracted cash flows plus refinancing gains can lift equity returns above 20% p.a. Answers which traffic and regulatory assumptions drive that. Readers can test an InvIT's distribution sustainability.

title: MSME Business Acquisition Returns
brief: Investigates acquiring MSME units in India at multiples implying owner-level returns above 20% p.a. Answers how buyers verify cash flows in informal settings. Readers can prepare a screening and valuation process for small-business purchases.

title: PMS Concentrated Small-Cap Strategies
brief: Investigates Indian portfolio-management strategies running concentrated small-cap mandates with above-20% p.a. ambitions, and the fee and liquidity terms attached. Answers how to compare them against a direct portfolio. Readers can evaluate a PMS proposal line by line.

title: What RBI Licensing Means for a P2P Platform
brief: Covers the licensing route for non-banking financial company peer-to-peer platforms, capital requirements and the rules binding them. Answers what regulatory protection a lender actually gains. Readers can verify a platform's licensed status before committing money.

title: The Platform Is Not the Lender: Legal Roles in P2P Lending
brief: Covers the tripartite relationship between platform, lender and borrower under the RBI framework, and what the platform may not do. Answers who holds the loan contract. Readers can identify where their legal claim sits in a dispute.

title: Escrow Account Mechanics in P2P Lending
brief: Covers the settlement and escrow structure through which lender funds reach borrowers and repayments return, including the permitted escrow arrangements. Answers how money moves without the platform handling it freely. Readers can follow their money through the pipeline.

title: Lender Exposure Limits Across Loans and Platforms
brief: Covers regulatory caps on how much one lender may lend to a single borrower and across platforms, and why the limits exist. Answers how diversification is enforced rather than merely advised. Readers can plan allocations that respect the framework.

title: The No-Guarantee Rule and the Credit-Enhancement Ban
brief: Covers the prohibition on platforms guaranteeing returns or providing credit enhancement, and the marketing language that works around it. Answers why any assured-return offer is a red flag. Readers can spot non-compliant propositions immediately.

title: Interest Arithmetic on P2P Loans: Reducing Balance Explained
brief: Covers how P2P loan interest is calculated on reducing balances, how instalments are split, and where platform fees enter the calculation. Answers what a quoted rate means for the lender's cash flow. Readers can verify a repayment schedule independently.

title: Amortisation Schedules and the Monthly Cash Flow of P2P
brief: Covers equated monthly instalment construction, the shifting principal-interest split and why lenders face continuous reinvestment decisions. Answers what cash a P2P portfolio throws off each month. Readers can plan reinvestment rather than accumulating idle balances.

title: How P2P Loans Are Underwritten in India
brief: Covers the borrower data platforms use, the role of bureau scores, income verification and the limits of algorithmic underwriting on small-ticket loans. Answers where underwriting quality gets tested. Readers can judge a platform's borrower-selection discipline.

title: Risk Grading Systems on P2P Platforms
brief: Covers how platforms grade borrower risk and map grades to indicative rates, and the gap between a grade and an observed default rate. Answers what a grade does not promise. Readers can compare grades against realised outcomes over time.

title: Borrower Verification and Documentation on P2P Platforms

title: The Pension System Architecture in India
brief: Covers the layered retirement landscape: provident funds, the national pension system, annuities and employer arrangements, and how the pieces interconnect. Answers which institutions hold which retirement money. Readers can map their own retirement stack.

title: Money Markets and Liquidity Plumbing
brief: Covers the participants and instruments of the Indian money market, and the channels through which central bank operations transmit to short-term rates. Answers how short-term liquidity circulates. Readers can interpret liquidity conditions from public data.

title: Government Borrowing and the Debt Programme
brief: Covers how central and state governments fund deficits through auctions and small savings, and how the borrowing calendar influences yields across the curve. Answers where the largest borrower in the market operates. Readers can connect fiscal news to bond markets.

title: The Foreign Exchange Market and Controls
brief: Covers the rupee's trading arrangements, authorised-dealer banking channels and the current-account and capital-account rules residents encounter. Answers how foreign currency legitimately enters and leaves India. Readers can navigate forex rules for personal transactions.

title: Credit Information and Bureaus
brief: Covers how credit bureaus collect and score borrower data, the free-report entitlement and the dispute process for incorrect entries. Answers who holds your credit record. Readers can audit and correct their own credit history.

title: Financial Conglomerates and Group Exposure
brief: Covers the groups that span banking, insurance, funds and lending, the contagion channels between arms and the supervision of interconnected entities. Answers why troubles in one arm affect others. Readers can identify group exposure in their holdings.

title: Financial Stability Monitoring
brief: Covers the purpose and content of financial stability assessments, the indicators monitored and how stress propagates through Indian institutions. Answers how systemic risk is tracked. Readers can read stability reports for themselves.

title: Corporate Bond Market Development in India
brief: Covers the efforts to deepen the corporate bond market, the investor base and infrastructure constraints involved and the reforms attempted. Answers why the market remains bank-dominated. Readers can assess bond-market policy debates.

title: What an Investment Return Actually Is
brief: Covers return as the change in claim on future consumption, the components of income, growth and revaluation, and the mistakes in casual return talk. Answers what is really being measured. Readers can define and compute returns precisely.

title: Nominal Returns and the Inflation Toll
brief: Covers why headline returns overstate progress, how inflation compounds against an investor and the discipline of thinking in real terms throughout. Answers what wealth growth means after purchasing power. Readers can restate every return in real terms.

title: Compounding Over Decades
brief: Covers the geometric accumulation of returns, the disproportionate weight of late contributions and the fragility imposed by interruptions. Answers why time dominates contribution size. Readers can reason about multi-decade compounding honestly.

title: Risk as the Price of Return
brief: Covers the proposition that higher expected returns must be earned by bearing risk, the exceptions where risk is uncompensated and the difference between risk and uncertainty. Answers why safe high returns invite suspicion. Readers can classify the risks in an offer.

title: Volatility Versus Permanent Loss
brief: Covers the distinction between quotational decline and destroyed capital, the situations in which each occurs and why confusing them misleads strategy. Answers which risk deserves avoidance. Readers can audit holdings for permanent-loss exposure.

title: Drawdowns and Recoveries
brief: Covers the anatomy of peak-to-trough declines, the asymmetric arithmetic of recovery and the behavioural tests drawdowns impose on long-horizon investors. Answers what a paper loss demands. Readers can plan behaviour before the next drawdown arrives.

title: Time Horizon and the Odds of Loss
brief: Covers how the probability of negative outcomes declines as horizons lengthen for volatile assets, and the limits of that comfort. Answers what horizons genuinely protect. Readers can align asset choice with time available.

title: Taxes as a Return Lever
brief: Covers how taxation of income, gains and transactions compounds against returns, and the legitimate levers of wrapper choice, timing and holding periods. Answers what can be improved after tax. Readers can identify their largest tax frictions.

title: Fees and the Quiet Return Killer
brief: Covers the cumulative cost of expense ratios, advice and churn, why percentage fees look small annually and large across decades, and how to compare products net. Answers what a fee is really worth. Readers can act on fee evidence.

title: Luck Versus Skill in Track Records
brief: Covers the statistical difficulty of distinguishing ability from randomness in return series, the number of observations needed and the base rates of persistence. Answers how much a track record proves. Readers can evaluate performance claims sceptically.

title: Survivorship Bias in Performance Data
brief: Covers how closed and merged funds vanish from databases, biasing averages upward, and how to detect the distortion. Answers why reported category returns flatter reality. Readers can interrogate performance data for missing failures.

title: Mean Reversion and Trend
brief: Covers both arguments: that extremes correct and that strength persists, the horizons and contexts in which each appears and the danger of applying either mechanically. Answers which force dominates when. Readers can classify evidence rather than pick a camp.

title: Valuations and Future Returns
brief: Covers the relationship between starting valuations and subsequent long-horizon returns, its noise at short horizons and its implications for expectation setting. Answers what high prices imply without pretending to forecast. Readers can adjust expected returns for starting conditions.

title: The Equity Risk Premium
brief: Covers the excess return demanded for holding equity over safe bonds, the estimation methods and the uncertainty around the number. Answers what premium a portfolio implicitly assumes. Readers can use the concept without false precision.

title: Return on Capital Versus Return of Capital
brief: Covers the difference between income earned and principal handed back, the distribution structures that disguise one as the other and the due diligence that reveals it. Answers what a payout actually is. Readers can test any yield claim.

title: Market Cycles and Human Psychology
brief: Covers the emotional sequence that accompanies expanding and contracting markets, the documented biases that amplify it and the procedures that counteract them. Answers why investors buy high and sell low. Readers can install personal circuit-breakers.

title: Long-Run Behaviour of Indian Asset Classes
brief: Covers the historical character of Indian equity, debt, gold and property returns, including the data limitations and what can and cannot be inferred. Answers what Indian investors can reasonably expect. Readers can set expectations grounded in the record.

title: Why Forecasts Fail, and What Planning Can Rely On
brief: Covers the track record of return, rate and price forecasts, the incentive structures that keep them coming and the few things more forecastable than prices. Answers what planning can rely on. Readers can replace forecasts with scenario ranges.

title: Perma-Bulls, Perma-Bears and the Cost of Certainty
brief: Covers the recurring market narratives of permanent optimism and doom, the careers built on each and the cost of following either to its conclusion. Answers what conviction untethered from evidence costs. Readers can evaluate market commentary by its incentive.

title: Compounding Requires Survival
brief: Covers the primacy of staying in the game: leverage, concentration and illiquidity as threats to survival, and the arithmetic of never recovering from zero. Answers what must be protected first. Readers can set hard limits that preserve participation.

title: Income Versus Total Return
brief: Covers the distinction between cash yield and all-in return, the psychological appeal of income and when that appeal is worth its cost. Answers whether a high-income strategy is really better. Readers can compare strategies on total return properly.

title: Building a Return Expectation Framework
brief: Covers assembling honest return expectations from observable inputs: starting yields, earnings growth, valuation change and costs, each with ranges. Answers what a portfolio can plausibly deliver. Readers can write expectations they will actually hold to.
